requirements.text: Questions are due 2026-09-14 at 11:00 AM ET.
The live Q&A session is scheduled for 2026-09-16 at 11:00 AM ET.
The Solution Concept Paper is due 2026-09-18 at 9:00 AM ET.
The mandatory template must be used; Sections 1 through 6 are limited to six pages.
The Concept Paper must address problem understanding, concept and vision, technical approach, IP/data rights, risk/opportunity, and ROM.
The performer must possess and maintain an active Top Secret Facility Clearance at Concept Paper submission.
All assigned personnel must be U.S. citizens with at least interim Secret clearance.
Privileged users of PII systems require final favorably adjudicated T5; interim T5/T5R or Top Secret may suffice to start.
Personnel must obtain CAC logical access and support virtual presentation of CAC certificate information.
The proposed participation structure must satisfy an applicable 10 U.S.C. 4022 prototype OTA eligibility path.
Existing Individual Engagement applications must remain available during development, integration, testing, demonstration, and evaluation.
The solution must provide a secure, scalable common entry point and unified user experience across modernized mission services.
The solution must support multiple approved identity and access management service providers and multiple MFA approaches including CAC/PIV and ECA.
Navigation and access control must account for user, user type, role, permission, attributes, data/resources, and least privilege.
The target must be modular and composable, with business rules separated from applications and API/event-driven integration supported.
The prototype must validate a hub-and-spoke model while underlying applications continue assigned functions.
Delivery must use modern DevSecOps practices and infrastructure as code.
Within the first 30 days of Phase 1, the vendor assumes sustainment responsibility for identified IE applications and integrations.
Sustainment includes operational support, incident and defect resolution, patching, release support, and security/authorization support.
Phase 1 establishes personas, roles/attributes, workflows, interface strategy, onboarding strategy, architecture, security, tests, backlog, success criteria, and sustainment baseline.
Phase 2 demonstrates the common entry point, role/attribute navigation, approved identity integration, dashboard, and at least one end-to-end workflow.
Phase 3 onboards eApp, IEP, required forms including PVQ/DD254 examples, and PDT while preserving operations.
Phase 3 must produce reusable onboarding patterns, interface specifications, and lessons learned.
Phase 4 supports GAT, UAT, regression, integration, performance, reliability, accessibility, and security testing as applicable.
Security authorization is integral throughout the prototype; a successful prototype achieves an ATO.
The performer produces authorization documentation/evidence and addresses security gaps or remediation actions.
Phase 4 produces production-readiness assessment, transition recommendation, phased production approach, and deployment/operations/sustainment/onboarding ROM.
Government data and PII handling must follow applicable privacy protections and responsible-AI constraints.
Enterprise data may not train, evaluate, or enhance external commercial foundation models or proprietary algorithms.
DCSA retains ownership of ingested data, curated products, fine-tuned model weights, and custom embeddings.
CUI and classified data must be processed, transmitted, and stored in accordance with 32 CFR Part 117 and DoD Manual 5200.01.
Project information, contract references, classification levels, and clearances may not be released in public promotional material.
Prototype evaluation uses existing IE applications in AWS GovCloud IL4; successful continuation is expected in the mission IL5 environment.
The prototype period is six months in four sequential phases, with potential extension for additional integrations or evaluation.
The Government plans one award but may make multiple awards or none; successful prototype completion may support follow-on OTA or FAR production.
